findings.title: Forward keyword arguments from the os.open spy
findings.trigger: Run the new evidence-copy test on Python 3.13 with fd-based shutil.rmtree cleanup.
findings.execution_path: The test patches runner.os.open, which changes the shared os module. execute() reaches its finally block and calls shutil.rmtree(); that calls os.open(..., dir_fd=dirfd), but _spy_open accepts only positional arguments.
findings.consequence: The test raises TypeError before reaching its evidence-copy flag assertion, causing the full test suite to fail. CI also uses Python 3.13 and runs this suite.
findings.evidence: The harness evidence for f46f18ccac125562f04f95a536634b9b8f17a9cc records this exact traceback at execute() cleanup: _spy_open() got an unexpected keyword argument 'dir_fd'. Result: 1 failed, 2399 passed. The failing test never reaches its intended O_CREAT/O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW assertion.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept **kwargs in _spy_open and forward them to real_open. Rerun the targeted test and the full suite.

limitations: Pytest was not rerun inside the read-only review sandbox. F001 was reproduced by the harness on the exact inspected head, as recorded in .codex-review-evidence/pytest.txt.
